proof:
Source. Step 1, (1a)–(1f), of the supplied proof of codim1_region_density_one_dense. It uses the C² embedded-submanifold definition of Simon Ch. 2, §4 and the orientation definition 6.2.2. Here it is stated for an arbitrary x ∈ N ∩ U, with the plane Π parametrised by an isometry ι. Siblings used: orientation_sign and unit_orientation_dual (accepted, reused).

Notation. e_1, …, e_{n+1} is the standard basis of ℝ^{n+1}. ι* is the adjoint of ι, so ι*ι = id and ι*h = 0 iff h ⊥ range ι. DG(v) := ι + Du(v) and J(v) := (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩])^{1/2}.

Proof.
1. (Tangent plane and ι; (1a).)
- IsOrientation at x gives a subspace Π with Π = tangentSpace(N, x) as sets, and an orthonormal τ = (τ_1, …, τ_{n+1}) spanning Π with ξN(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξN(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α.
- In the second case replace τ_1 by −τ_1. This keeps τ orthonormal with the same span, and α(−τ_1, τ_2, …) = −α(τ). So ξN(x)(α) = α(τ_1, …, τ_{n+1}) for all α, and dim Π = n + 1.
- Let ι be the linear isometry with ι(e_i) = τ_i; its range is Π.
2. (The chart is a homeomorphism; (1b).)
- IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+1) N at x gives open V ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} and open W ∋ x, and ψ with: ψ C² and injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective on V. Fix z₀ ∈ V with ψ(z₀) = x.
- Claim: if C ⊆ V is relatively closed, then ψ(C) is closed in W. Let c_k ∈ C with ψ(c_k) → q ∈ W. Then K := {q} ∪ {ψ(c_k)} is a compact subset of W, so the c_k lie in the compact set V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K). A subsequence converges to some c ∈ V; c ∈ C, and ψ(c) = q.
- So ψ : V → W ∩ N is a closed continuous bijection, i.e. a homeomorphism. In particular ψ(V₀) is relatively open in W ∩ N for every open V₀ ⊆ V.
3. (Range of Dψ(z₀); (1c).) For a ∈ ℝ^{n+1} choose ε > 0 with z₀ + εta ∈ V for |t| < 1.
- γ(t) := ψ(z₀ + εta) is C¹ on (−1, 1), maps into N, γ(0) = x and γ′(0) = εDψ(z₀)a. So Dψ(z₀)a ∈ Π, since Π is a subspace.
- Dψ(z₀) is injective and dim Π = n + 1, so range Dψ(z₀) = Π.
4. (Graph map; (1d).)
- φ := ι*∘(ψ − x) is C² on V with φ(z₀) = 0, and Dφ(z₀) = ι*Dψ(z₀) is invertible (ι* is injective on Π). By the C² inverse function theorem (Mathlib ContDiffAt.to_localInverse) there are an open V₀ with z₀ ∈ V₀ ⊆ V and an open O ∋ 0 such that φ : V₀ → O is bijective with C² inverse.
- Put u(v) := ψ(φ^{-1}(v)) − x − ι v on O and u := 0 off O. Then ι*u = 0 on O, so (★) ψ(φ^{-1}(v)) = x + ι v + u(v) with u(v) ⊥ range ι.
- u is C² on O and u(0) = 0. Also Du(0) = (I − ιι*)Dψ(z₀)Dφ(z₀)^{-1} = 0, because range Dψ(z₀) = Π.
- By step 2 there is s > 0 with B_s(x) ⊆ W and N ∩ B_s(x) ⊆ ψ(V₀).
- Choose r₁ > 0 with closedBall(x, 2r₁) ⊆ U ∩ B_s(x), and put δ₂ := r₁. Then choose δ₁ ∈ (0, r₁) with ball(0, δ₁) ⊆ O, ‖Du‖ ≤ 1 and ‖u‖ < δ₂/2 on ball(0, δ₁); this uses continuity of u and Du at 0.
5. (Properties other than orientation.)
(a) closedBall(x, δ₁ + δ₂) ⊆ closedBall(x, 2r₁) ⊆ U.
(b) u(0) = 0, and u is C² on ball(0, δ₁) ⊆ O.
(c) For v ∈ ball(0, δ₁): u(v) ⊥ range ι, ‖Du(v)‖ ≤ 1, ‖u(v)‖ < δ₂/2, and x + ι v + u(v) = ψ(φ^{-1}(v)) ∈ N by (★).
(d) If ‖v‖ < δ₁, ‖h‖ < δ₂, h ⊥ range ι and q := x + ι v + h ∈ N, then ‖q − x‖² = ‖v‖² + ‖h‖², so ‖q − x‖ < 2r₁ < s. Hence q = ψ(z) with z ∈ V₀. Then φ(z) = ι*(q − x) = v, so z = φ^{-1}(v), and (★) gives h = u(v).
6. (Orientation; (1e)–(1f).) Let D := ball(0, δ₁), G(v) := x + ι v + u(v) (C² on D), and fix v ∈ D.
(6a) u maps the open set D into the closed subspace (range ι)^⊥, so Du(v)a ⊥ range ι. Hence ‖DG(v)a‖² = ‖a‖² + ‖Du(v)a‖² ≥ ‖a‖², and DG(v) is injective. Therefore J(v) > 0, and J is continuous on D.
(6b) IsOrientation at G(v) ∈ N gives Q_v = tangentSpace(N, G(v)) with dim Q_v = n + 1, of which ξN(G(v)) is a unit orientation. The curves t ↦ G(v + εta) are C¹, lie in N, pass through G(v) and have velocity εDG(v)a. So range DG(v) ⊆ Q_v, and equality holds by dimension.
(6c) Let a_i := DG(v)e_i and η(v)(α) := α(a_1, …, a_{n+1})/J(v). Gram–Schmidt gives an orthonormal basis σ of Q_v and an upper-triangular R with positive diagonal such that a_j = Σ_{i≤j} R_{ij}σ_i. Then α(a) = det R·α(σ), the Gram matrix is RᵀR, and J(v) = det R. So η(v)(α) = α(σ), and η(v) is a unit orientation of Q_v.
(6d) By orientation_sign, ξN(G(v)) = ±η(v).
(6e) Let L be the map from unit_orientation_dual in degree n+1, so η(v)(L(η(v))) = 1. Put s(v) := ξN(G(v))(L(η(v))); then s(v) = ±1, according to the sign in (6d). s is continuous on D:
- ξN is continuous on N and G is continuous from D into N, so v ↦ ξN(G(v)) is continuous;
- v ↦ η(v) is continuous, because (b_i) ↦ (α ↦ α(b_1, …, b_{n+1})) is continuous multilinear, v ↦ a_i is continuous and 1/J is continuous;
- L is continuous linear, and evaluation is continuous bilinear.
D is connected and s takes values in {±1}, so s is constant. At v = 0: G(0) = x, DG(0) = ι, a_i = τ_i, J(0) = 1 and η(0) = ξN(x), so s(0) = 1. Hence ξN(G(v)) = η(v), i.e. ξN(x + ι v + u(v))(α)·J(v) = α(ι e_1 + Du(v)e_1, …, ι e_{n+1} + Du(v)e_{n+1}) for all α and all v ∈ D.
Steps 5 and 6 give every conjunct. ∎
key_steps: Pick an orthonormal basis τ of Π = T_xN with ξN(x) = +τ_1∧…∧τ_{n+1}, and the isometry ι with ι e_i = τ_i.
Properness makes the chart ψ a homeomorphism onto W ∩ N, and range Dψ(z₀) = Π.
The inverse function theorem for ι*(ψ − x) gives the C² graph map u (u(0) = 0, Du(0) = 0, u ⊥ Π); N near x is its graph, and δ₁ is shrunk to get the bounds.
Along the graph, T_{G(v)}N = DG(v)ℝ^{n+1}, and the Gram–Schmidt multivector η(v) is a unit orientation of it.
orientation_sign together with the continuous sign s(v) = ξN(G v)(L η(v)) (unit_orientation_dual) on the connected ball gives ξN(G v)·J(v) = DG(v)-pushforward of e_1∧…∧e_{n+1}.
